questions.q: What are the three real limitations of authoring directly against the Data Factory service without Git?
options: No draft state, no real collaboration/review model, and no ARM template for the factory itself
It's slower, costs more, and requires a special license
It only works with SQL Server sources
There are no real limitations — Git integration is purely optional convenience
questions.explain: Without Git, every change publishes immediately with no way to save a draft, there's no code review workflow, and there's no ARM template representing the factory itself.

questions.q: Which branch can you actually publish from in a Git-connected data factory?
options: Only the collaboration branch (main by default)
Any feature branch, directly
Only the adf_publish branch
Publishing doesn't require being on any particular branch
questions.explain: Publish is only available from the collaboration branch — feature branches let you save and iterate, but changes must be merged into the collaboration branch before they can be published.

questions.q: What does publishing actually generate, and where does it go?
options: ARM templates representing the published factory state, written to the adf_publish branch
A compiled binary written to the collaboration branch
Nothing is generated — publishing only updates the live service directly with no artifact
A new GitHub repository is created for every publish
questions.explain: Publishing generates ARM templates and writes them to a separate publish branch (adf_publish by default), which is what CI/CD release pipelines actually deploy from.

questions.q: Is the collaboration branch always a live reflection of what's actually running in the Data Factory service?
options: No — it must be published manually (or via automation) before changes take effect
Yes, always, automatically and instantly
Only if the factory has fewer than ten pipelines
Yes, but only for GitHub-connected factories, not Azure Repos
questions.explain: Merging to the collaboration branch alone doesn't deploy anything — an explicit Publish action (or automated release pipeline) is required to make those changes live.

questions.q: What happens when you save a linked service using a raw password instead of a Key Vault reference?
options: It publishes immediately to the live service, bypassing the normal Git branch-and-publish workflow
It's automatically converted to a Key Vault reference
The save is rejected entirely until Key Vault is configured
It behaves identically to any other resource, going through the normal Git flow
questions.explain: Data Factory never writes secrets into Git — a non-Key-Vault-backed credential publishes immediately upon save, for that one resource only, precisely to avoid ever committing a secret to source control.
